newsitem.title: USA: Stock market quiet ahead of Fed policy-setting meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stock market quiet ahead of Fed policy-setting meeting.

text.p: Stock prices were steady Monday as investors held their breath ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on Tuesday.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 7.01 points at 7,201.68, regaining its footing after tumbling nearly 140 points Friday on strong economic news that revived fears of higher interest rates.

In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on moderate volume of 178 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange. The Nasdaq composite index dipped 0.51 of a point to 1,340.22.
"Everyone is holding their breath before the FOMC (Fed) meeting," said Frank Calta, a trader at Dain Bosworth.

The Federal Open Market Committee, the central bank's policy-making arm which sets short-term rates, meets Tuesday amid mixed views as to whether it will raise interest rates again. On March 25, the Fed raised interest rates by a quarter percentage point in an effort to head off possible inflationary pressure.
The stock market was expected to stay quiet until the outcome of the Fed meeting is known, possibly by mid-afternoon Tuesday.
"It's not as busy as last week and we're not seeing many new situations, like you normally see on Monday," Calta said.

Business was also slow in bonds, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond off 5/32, which lowered its yield to 6.90 percent from 6.91 percent at Friday's close. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"Nobody is willing to take big bets the day before a Fed meeting," Calta said.
James Melcher, president of Balestra Capital, said, "The concern du jour is the Fed."

If the Fed lets short-term rates stand, analysts said the stock market could get a quick bounce. But analysts were less certain about market reaction if the Fed raises rates by a quarter points or more.
"Economists and strategists are almost split down the middle about whether the Fed will raise rates," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"But investors expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged. If the Fed does raise rates, it will be a big surprise to markets," he said.
Others said the market had already braced itself for a quarter-point hike and would take it in stride.
"After all, what's a quarter-point hike?," Melcher said. "The (Fed) meeting is not that big an event anymore."
Among individual stocks, recent high-flyer International Business Machines Corp. lost 1-7/8 to 168.
"Many of the technology stocks are weaker," one trader said. "I think money is coming out of mutual funds in the tech sector, which is pulling them down. But trading is quiet."

Oracle Corp. was off 3/8 to 44, after the company said it signed a definitive agreement with Netscape Communications Corp. to merge Netscape's Navio Communciations, with Oracle's Network Computer Inc. Netscape was up 1-1/8 at 30-3/8.
Freemont General Corp. rose 2 to 30-5/8 after the company said it would buy the workers compensation insurance carrier, Industrial Indemnity Holdings Inc. from a unit of Xerox Corp.
